obligations.description: Dimension three and the fixed invariant coframe/probability are explicit for the mass statements.
The normalized probability family in the density theorem is specific to the exact Iwasawa quotient.
The i/(2pi) complex-Hessian normalization gives positive ddC theta_A with coefficient1/(4pi^2).
Diagonalization expresses ddC theta_A as positive (2,0)-form squares; in dimension three these are nonnegative (2,2)-forms.
Balancedness and the internal threefold maximum theorem give upper mass H det A for all bounded potentials.
The density-extrema theorem and invariant determinant formula give an attained, rather than merely supremal, density maximum.
Metric independence turns this finite upper mass into BMP on the compact quotient.
A bounded theta_A potential is also theta_(A+epsilon I)-plurisubharmonic.
For singular semipositive A the determinant bound tends to zero.
Multilinear bounded products give a polynomial in epsilon with finite mixed coefficients, proving convergence of total mass.
Positivity makes the entire bounded limiting top measure zero.
Semipositivity admits the constant canonical cutoff; restrictions of its zero products give zero non-pluripolar top product for unbounded potentials.
The Iwasawa lattice preserves the base projection; its fibers are connected central elliptic quotients.
Integration over the fundamental cube gives p_*mu0 equal to normalized base Haar probability.
The positive block matrix has a positive Schur complement and determinant a det S.
The base Kähler volume is2 det S/pi^2 in the book normalization.
The smooth equation theorem on the closed base fixes the scalar to zero by Stokes and the probability normalization.
The base determinant equation and Schur positivity produce a strictly positive lifted form.
The lifted top volume is H det A times the prescribed fiber-invariant probability.
Horizontal ddC potentials wedge the Iwasawa torsion to zero, so the lifted solution is balanced.
The dual formula and degree-two D_mu homogeneity produce the unique normalized minimizing metric and its exact probability volume.
The exact Iwasawa ddC theta_A is A33 tau1 wedge tau2; h0^3 is6 tau1 wedge tau2 wedge tau3.
The vertical gradient wedge ratio is A33|Z3u|^2/6, so mass variation has coefficient A33H/2.
For each arbitrary smooth probability, its normalized smooth solution realizes its variational volume as total mass.
Equality with the upper mass is equivalent to the global vertical derivative vanishing.
Realness of the potential kills both real vertical directions; connected fibers and smooth local sections give a smooth base potential.
The coefficient determinant of a lifted base potential descends to the base, forcing the maximizing probability to be fiber invariant.
Conversely every fiber-invariant probability is realized by the closed base equation, proving the full maximizer classification.
For a fixed base density f the determinant formula holds for every positive A, allowing differentiation without varying the reference.
The identical coefficient Hessian transfers only the matrix completion/bounds part of the earlier proof, without transferring invariant minimizing forms.
Coefficient means are taken against invariant mu0 and equal A divided by the determinant root; they are not pointwise form identities.
Unbounded normalized coefficient means preclude a fixed global h0 upper bound on the actual minimizing metrics.
A localized real bump with nonzero vertical derivative admits small two-sided strictly positive perturbations.
Its normalized probability has the exact quadratic volume deficit; it is constructed for fixed A and does not supply an arbitrary-density Hessian calculation.
General P15, arbitrary fiber-varying fixed densities, positive lower mass and spatial metric completeness are not inferred.
